title: Thursday Teacher Plan
note: Thursday = build day for every grade. Friday = finish, test, and the one turn-in. Openers are now Blooket.

4th Period.topic: Factory Method: build your brick factory
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, my live game has a BrickFactory that builds a row of my new bricks, and my exit ticket is turned in on Google Classroom.
4th Period.exitTicket: What you built today: your brick type and how you verified it in your live game.
prep: Blooket quiz loaded (or skip if not ready)
Thursday V2 doc posted with the Factory Pattern assignment
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Launch the review quiz on Tuesday's plan: attributes, selection logic, instance.
segments.why: Spiral review of the vocabulary they build with today.
tips: Start it before the bell.

segments.title: Points reminder
segments.do: Due Sunday: live game link, the brick plan (Tuesday's exit ticket), and a row of new bricks in the live game. Today only the exit ticket is turned in.
segments.why: Maslow: safety first, so students know what counts before they start.
tips: Say: if the game breaks, the plan and link still count.

segments.title: AI prompting and code setup
segments.do: Model the Copilot prompt from the doc: add selection logic to makeBrick(x, y, type) for their own type.
segments.why: Students design, AI writes code: the assessed skill is the mechanic, not the syntax.
tips: Have them paste their Tuesday plan into the prompt so the AI builds THEIR brick.
Their type must not be the worked example's 'strong'.

segments.title: You do: build the BrickFactory
segments.do: Students add the if-statement for their type, set 2 attributes, and make one row use it.
segments.why: Bloom Apply/Create: their own design inside the closed box.
tips: Most common bug: makeBricks() never passes the type, so every brick is default.
If drawBricks() ignores brick.color, the color won't show: have them ask the AI to draw with brick.color.
Early finishers: 3rd brick type (Future Engineer).

segments.title: Commit, Sync, hard refresh, check
segments.do: Commit, Sync Changes, open the live link, hard refresh, look for the new row.
segments.why: Only the live game proves it works.
tips: Pages can take a minute to update. Refresh again before panicking.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students submit the 1–2 sentence exit ticket on Google Classroom using the frames in the doc.
segments.why: The only turn-in today; Friday is the link turn-in.
tips: Read both frames aloud. Allow dictation.

watchFor: AI rewriting files outside bricks.js: re-prompt to only change makeBrick.
Syntax errors from a missing comma in the returned brick object: F12 console.
Students waiting on you: point to the Stuck table first.

6th Period.topic: TinkerCAD Truss Bridge: span the gap
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my bridge has a top chord, is grouped into one object, and is lifted 20 mm so it spans a 60 mm gap between two cubes.
6th Period.exitTicket: What number did you type to lift your bridge, and why that number?
prep: TinkerCAD open on the projector with Tuesday's deck + triangles
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Launch the 7th grade review: deck, Align, lifting with the black cone.
segments.why: Spiral review of Tuesday's tools before using them again.
tips: Note the most-missed question.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review misses, then read the goal: top chord, group, lift 20, span the gap.
segments.why: Front-load the goal before screens.
tips: Show the bridge-on-cubes picture from the handout.

segments.title: We do: add the top chord
segments.do: Box 80 × 20 × 2 → lift 22 → select all → L → middle dots.
segments.why: Fully worked round with numbers they type.
tips: 22 = 2 (deck) + 20 (triangle height). Say the math out loud.

segments.title: We do: group it and lift it
segments.do: Ctrl + A → Ctrl + G → black cone → type 20.
segments.why: Group first, then lift, or only one piece moves.
tips: Watch for students who lift before grouping: Ctrl + Z.

segments.title: You do: build the two cubes
segments.do: Box under the left end (20 × 20 × 20), Align left dot with the bridge; Box under the right end, Align right dot.
segments.why: Bloom Apply: they repeat Align on their own to make the span.
tips: Early finishers: longer span or second side (Future Engineer).

segments.title: Check from the front and side
segments.do: Students spin the view: deck on top of both cubes, gap underneath, nothing floating.
segments.why: Self-check before the exit ticket.
tips: Circulate to anyone who had sign-in trouble earlier in the week.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: What number did you type to lift your bridge, and why?
segments.why: Answered directly by what they did: 20, because the cubes are 20 tall.
tips: Read the frames aloud. Allow dictation.

watchFor: Bridge lifted before grouping: only the deck moves.
Cubes not aligned to the ends: deck hangs off one side.
Students who never finished Tuesday's deck: get them there first, then lift.

7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group has built both side trusses from our plan, every piece measured with our stick, and joined them with cross pieces if we have time.
7th Period.exitTicket: Why did your group lay every strip on top of your drawing before gluing it?
prep: Group bags (plans + measuring sticks) ready to hand back
Cardboard, scissors, glue out per group
Shelf space cleared for bridges to dry flat
Exit ticket posted on Google Classroom

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Launch the 6th grade review: the stick unit, equilateral, cut length, 12 diagonals.
segments.why: Spiral review of the plan they build from today.
tips: Hand back group bags after the quiz.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Review misses, then read the goal.
segments.why: Front-load a long hands-on period.
tips: Hold up a good plan from Tuesday (assign competence).

segments.title: Roles by birthday
segments.do: Youngest: Side Truss 1 Builder. Second youngest: Side Truss 2 Builder. Second oldest: Materials Manager. Oldest: Checker. Group of 3: oldest also Materials Manager. Group of 5: two youngest share Side Truss 1.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: every role is needed; no one decides who does what.
tips: Checker has real authority: nothing is glued until they check it.

segments.title: I do: one piece, start to finish
segments.do: Trace with the stick along the flutes, mark drawn length + a glue square at each end, cut, Checker checks, lay it on its line on the drawing.
segments.why: Fully worked round 1: one diagonal.
tips: Show the drawing as a jig: if the strip sits on the line, the triangle is right.

segments.title: You do: build on top of the drawing
segments.do: Builders: bottom chord → 6 diagonals → top chord for their side. Materials Manager: 4 cross pieces. Checker + MM: stand both sides ¼ stick apart and glue cross pieces at the bottom joints.
segments.why: Bloom Apply/Create: turning a plan into a structure.
tips: Bottom chord too long for the cardboard? 2 strips joined with a glue square.
Press each glue square 30 seconds.
If time runs out before joining, that's fine: joining is Friday's first step.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Why did you lay every strip on top of the drawing before gluing?
segments.why: Checks the idea of a jig: accurate, matching sides.
tips: Good answer: so the triangles come out equal and both sides match the plan.

segments.title: Clean up + set to dry
segments.do: Scraps in bin, tools back, bridge flat on the shelf with the bag.
segments.why: Glue sets overnight for Friday's load test.
tips: Count scissors back in.

watchFor: Glue sticks may be too weak for cardboard: test one joint early; if it fails, switch to whatever stronger glue you have.
Strips cut across the flutes (they crush).

accommodations: Agenda on the board, goal reviewed after the quiz, chunked numbered steps, worked example before you do, checklists, sentence frames, frequent check-ins.
Words tied to pictures (top chord, deck, gap; glue square, cut list). Partner talk before writing. Two sentence frames per exit ticket.
Lexend Deca handouts. Read steps aloud. Text-to-speech and speech-to-text OK. Spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer. 6th is hands-on all period with clear roles. If/then for non-preferred steps. Fidgets, break pass.
Dictation on the exit ticket. Shortened floor: 8th one changed attribute; 7th lifts the bridge onto cubes without the top chord; 6th builds one triangle on the drawing. Supportive group placement.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL), pick one for 1 KB point.
frameworks: Build day: every grade turns its plan into the week's product.
6th: birthday-order roles with real authority (Checker). 7th and 8th: shoulder partners for help.
Same routine, one exit ticket only, points known up front, worked example first.
All grades at Apply/Create: building their own designs.
